MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Platform Engineering | QA Automation Engineer
marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience and recent focus on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and has built short-lived Kubernetes test environments deployed through Helm. Experienced in improving pipeline performance, maintaining automated test infrastructure, and supporting teams with clear internal documentation. Seeking to move into a DevOps or platform engineering role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure and delivery: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level work and k3s homelab), Terraform (personal project), Argo CD
Monitoring and systems: Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL, Git
Programming and testing: Python, Bash, SQL, Java (test code), pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams of approximately 25 developers, covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into a dedicated stage.
- Built merge-request test environments using Docker Compose and later Helm charts deployed to a shared Kubernetes cluster; environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky test rate from 7% to under 1%.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling to seed test data in PostgreSQL.
- Wrote the internal guide to how CI works, which is used in onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal project | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Set up short-lived environments for each merge request, with the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data deployed via Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI.
- Configured automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity; QA and product teams can review features and run end-to-end tests before merge.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines for three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and separated end-to-end tests into a dedicated stage.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner cost by approximately 30%.

Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023
- Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team.
- Helped teams identify test failures to address; the flaky test rate fell from 7% to under 1%.

EDUCATION
BEng Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATION AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam booked for January 2027, not yet passed

LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)
docs.cover_letter:
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role. My experience is rooted in building dependable delivery and test infrastructure: at Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and built merge-request environments deployed with Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster. The role’s focus on taking infrastructure for a new train fleet from design toward production is a compelling opportunity to apply that platform work in a new domain.

The work I have delivered has measurable outcomes. I reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner cost by approximately 30% through parallelisation, dependency caching and pipeline restructuring. I also developed short-lived environments with PostgreSQL and seeded data, automated their cleanup, and maintained a roughly 900-test end-to-end suite whose flaky rate fell from 7% to under 1%. These projects have involved making test and deployment workflows usable for product teams, and I documented how our CI works for onboarding.

My Kubernetes experience is at the workload level: Odrava’s platform team operates the shared cluster, while I have namespace-level access and build Helm charts for test environments. Separately, my personal homelab uses k3s, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana and Loki, and I have provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform. My AWS experience is limited to personal learning of EC2 and S3 basics. I would bring this practical, transparent foundation in automation, observability and Linux-based environments to Corvale’s infrastructure work, while continuing to deepen my platform engineering skills.

Corvale’s new fleet connectivity work brings together cloud services and physical vehicles, and I would welcome the chance to discuss how my experience improving CI/CD and Kubernetes-based test environments could contribute to the team. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Marta Kowal-Brandt
